gap: No result ChatGPT got states that in Redragon's wireless combos the big 'Max DPI' number is not what the mouse can reach from its own buttons, or which combos use one receiver for both keyboard and mouse. On the S168 the headline says 12,800 DPI but the top on-board step is 8,000; the S136 says 7,200 and its top step is 7,200. Redragon says the S136, S144 and BS8773 share one 2.4 GHz dongle, but the S168 description never says so.
standout_why: I compared four pages. keyboardverdict.com gives no polling rate, no lights-off battery figure and no receiver sharing for any combo. mechkeyfoundry.com says only the Logitech pair shares a receiver (Logi Bolt) and gives the backlight on/off battery split only for the MX Mechanical Mini. gamingreviewguide.com gives no polling, battery or receiver details and says the S101-3 PRO DPI figures 'differ' without explaining why. None of the three covers the Redragon S136, S168 or BS8773 that ChatGPT showed as cards, and none splits headline DPI from the on-board top step or confirms which Redragon combos use one dongle. deskfinds.com returned 403 and I could not read it.
decides: This mostly confirms the pick rather than changing it. At $59.99 both the S136 (K628 + M693) and the S168 (K673 PRO + M693) are tri-mode 75% mechanical combos. Only the S136 page says one shared dongle serves both, and its 7,200 DPI headline is a real on-board step. The S168's 12,800 DPI needs Redragon's software, since its buttons stop at 8,000. For a shopper who wants a single USB receiver and specs that hold without software, the S136 is the cleaner $60 pick. The $36.99 BS8773 also uses one shared dongle, but it has low-profile switches (Redragon cuts the height by 30%) and its mouse tops out at 2,400 DPI, so it suits office use more than gaming. In the premium tier, Keychron is the only maker here that states one dongle controls both devices and a 1,000 Hz mouse polling rate (K2 HE + M3, $179.99). But it rates the mouse battery only in Bluetooth mode (95 h), so that figure is not comparable with the keyboard's unqualified 110 h.
